research_goldbach.touch_once_checkbox: One touch per n is enough (check existence only, don't count all sums)
research_goldbach.hint: Enter any integer n -- Pmax is derived automatically as the largest prime <= n. Checks every even number in [4, 2*Pmax] for a decomposition into a sum of two primes (windowCovered from Structural.lean). "Touch once" mode only searches for existence (stops at the first witness found) -- the paper's active line of proof. "All combinations" mode computes the full repCount(n) for every even number -- the counting framing, kept in the formalization only for comparison, since it inherits the parity problem.
research_goldbach.lean_repo_link: Lean 4 formalization of this tab on GitHub (proofs, zero "sorry") →
research_goldbach.viz_range_hint: "to" plays the old n field's role -- Pmax (largest prime <= to) is derived from it, and it's also the scan's own upper bound. "from" defaults to 4, but can be changed -- it must be >=4 and at least 2 less than "to" (so at least one even number fits in the range). A narrower range scans faster for large values.

research_goldbach.summary_truncated: (showing the first {shown} of {total} rows in the table -- full results available via Export CSV)
research_goldbach.viz_hint: Draws the window [4, Pmax+2] (Pmax = largest prime <= n) -- exactly the range the Lean lemma "additiveSelfContained_of_hasGoldbachRep" proves unconditionally. Primes are read from storage (across every floor needed), not recomputed. Both p and q are required <= Pmax here -- there is no separate "q may be new" mode anymore, this is the one, more general window.
research_goldbach.error_storage_missing: Storage is missing floor {floor} up to at least {upto} -- generate that range (Generation tab, floor {floor}) and try again.

research_goldbach.viz_status_shown: Showing window for n={n} (Pmax={pmax}). Change n above and check again.
research_goldbach.viz_subheader: The old base (blue, primes <= Pmax) supplies BOTH summands (p and q) for EVERY even number shown below -- window narrowed to [4, Pmax+2], because that's exactly the range where Lean (additiveSelfContained_of_hasGoldbachRep, SelfContainment.lean) proves unconditionally: if any representation of n exists at all, both summands are <= Pmax.
research_goldbach.viz_q_new_note: q > Pmax -- not needed for p
research_goldbach.viz_legend_new_q: both summands (p and q) share the same blue -- here BOTH must be <= Pmax, that's a proven requirement (Lean), not just information
research_goldbach.viz_summary_covered: Segment covered -- all {segment_size} new even numbers built from the old base alone.
research_goldbach.error_decompose_no_win: Check the window first (the "Sprawdz okno" button above) to establish a Pmax to compare against.
research_goldbach.error_decompose_must_b: The number to decompose must be even and >= 4.
research_goldbach.decompose_verdict_yes: buildableFromBase(Pmax={pmax}) [Lean, Constructive.lean] CONFIRMED: every one of the {count} pairs has p <= Pmax -- that is exactly Lean's own criterion (exists p q, p <= B and ...), which only ever bounds p, never q. For n inside the window [4, 2*Pmax] this is a PROVEN arithmetic fact (p <= n/2 <= Pmax), not just an observation.
research_goldbach.decompose_verdict_no: buildableFromBase(Pmax={pmax}) [Lean, Constructive.lean] NOT confirmed -- this number lies OUTSIDE the window [4, 2*Pmax] for this Pmax, so the p <= n/2 <= Pmax proof doesn't apply here; none of the {count} pairs has p <= Pmax.

primality.hint: Check primality runs three independent tests (Miller-Rabin, Fermat, Solovay-Strassen) against the same number -- Fermat and Solovay-Strassen are deliberately shown next to Miller-Rabin even though they're weaker (Fermat fails on Carmichael numbers), so that difference is visible. const_records.hint: Scans THIS project's OWN storage (constellations/kK/variantID/, not pzktupel.de) for the selected k -- shows the smallest offset found per floor and variant. The "Floor from/to" fields (optional, leave blank for no bound) limit the scan to a specific floor range instead of the whole storage -- useful when storage is large and the full table gets unreadable. Double-click a cell to see the full list of hits for that floor and variant below the table. PDF/CSV export includes every individual hit (not just the smallest offset) for the currently displayed floor range. An asterisk (*) means the floor matches the digit count of a known global record from the pattern catalog -- that's a floor coincidence, NOT confirmation it's the same number (the catalog doesn't store the record's exact offset).

quick.intro: Enter a floor or a number range to generate -- the app will translate it into the window width and window count in the form below (window width capped at 10,000,000).
quick.hint_floor: If the floor doesn't exist yet, it will be created. Width is a multiple of 10 million (1 = 10M, max 1000 = 10B) -- the requested amount is always rounded up to whole windows, on-disk files stay the same predictable size. Empty starting point = continue from the last existing file (then type the Floor field yourself); a given starting point determines the floor for you (the field becomes read-only) and sets a LITERAL target -- the app checks whether [starting point, starting point + width) is already in storage and reports that instead of regenerating it; if only part is missing, it generates just that part.
quick.hint_range: Both fields are required, From cannot be greater than or equal to To, minimum value for From is 0. Python-style formats allowed, e.g. 10**5. The range is rounded out to whole windows: From rounded down, To rounded up to the nearest multiple of 10,000,000 (e.g. 12M..309M -> 10M..310M). Must fit within a single floor -- the engine generates one floor at a time. If the given range is already fully in storage, the app will say so; if only partially, it will generate the missing part (from the last existing file through the end of the requested range).
quick.explore_auto_floor_empty: Nothing has been generated yet anywhere in this database -- type a floor yourself to start exploring one.
quick.hint_explore: Leave Floor blank (or click its own "Auto (highest floor)" button, which fills it in explicitly) to continue from wherever the deepest generated data in the whole database currently sits -- re-detected fresh every time, so pressing Generate repeatedly with nothing typed keeps extending whatever is genuinely deepest right now. Type a floor yourself to explore a specific one instead; this mode only ever continues an EXISTING floor (it never creates a new one), so a completely empty database still needs one typed by hand. A low floor (0-6, 0 is a real floor here, not a stand-in for blank) is a small, fixed range shared by all of them together: if it isn't fully generated yet, one click fills it completely (Iterations/Width don't apply to it) and stops there; if it's ALREADY fully generated, this mode automatically rolls forward to floor 7 instead and continues using the Iterations/Width you asked for -- there's nothing left below floor 7 to explore, ever. Width is a multiple of 10 million PER iteration (1 = 10M, max 1000 = 10B, same meaning as Floor only's) -- size it to the available RAM (see ITS OWN Auto button, further right). Number of iterations is how many times that width gets added in a row (max 100).
quick.hint_primesieve: Floor + From + Width, not From/To -- From is a literal starting point (like Floor mode's own Starting point field), Width is a multiple of 10 million added to it (same [1, 1000] meaning as Floor/Exploration mode's Width). Floor is independent of From -- type a floor and click Auto to fill From with wherever that floor's storage currently ends, without having to work out a huge resume number by hand; leaving From blank and just entering a Floor does the same thing automatically when you click Generate. Generation runs through libprimesieve's own primesieve_generate_primes() directly, with no batching/orchestrator of ours involved -- the fastest way to fill a range, within libprimesieve's own uint64 limit (up to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615). Requesting anything past that limit truncates the result to it; use Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead for numbers beyond it (slower, but with no such ceiling).

quick.note_truncated_floor_boundary: NOTE: the requested range extended past this floor's boundary -- generation was capped at {boundary} (the floor's end). The rest was skipped; generate it separately on the next floor.

quick.note_width_capped_alignment: NOTE: the given starting point doesn't sit on a window boundary (10M) -- to avoid exceeding the set Width by even one window, the end of the range was trimmed slightly (by less than one window) instead of rounded up.
